key_insight: LEGO replaces explicit 3D lifting with a lifting-free pipeline for exocentric-to-egocentric video generation. By avoiding rigid point-cloud reconstruction, it aims to better handle the large view gap and missing target-view content.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of generating an egocentric video from a single exocentric recording, where the two camera viewpoints have little overlap and much of the desired first-person view is never directly observed.
method: Use a lifting-free approach instead of estimating depth and reconstructing an explicit 3D point cloud.
Condition a video diffusion model without relying on deterministic pixel-to-point reprojected mappings.
Target the novel-view synthesis problem more robustly when the target egocentric view is heavily unobserved in the input exocentric video.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a simpler and potentially more robust alternative to depth-based view synthesis pipelines. It may reduce failure modes caused by imperfect geometry estimation and improve realism in cross-view video generation.

paper_title: LEGO: A Lifting-Free Approach for Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
